standard_prerequisites.use: The canonical map and six-term sequence of Modules, Lemma exact-sequence-NL-ringed-topoi, the affine description of naive cotangent complexes (lemma-NL-affine, same chapter), and the algebra transitivity result for lci morphisms (More on Algebra); cited inputs with the reduction written in the retained span.

core_obligations: Reduce the construction of the triangle to showing that the canonical map f^*NL_{Y/Z} -> Cone(NL_{X/Z} -> NL_{X/Y})[-1] of the Modules lemma is an isomorphism.
Reduce further, via the six-term exact sequence, to injectivity of H^{-1}(f^*NL_{Y/Z}) -> H^{-1}(NL_{X/Z}).
Verify the injectivity affine locally using lemma-NL-affine to translate into algebra, and conclude with the algebra transitivity lemma for complete intersection morphisms.

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the triangle to the vanishing of the canonical map and then to left injectivity in the six-term sequence.
Verify the injectivity affine locally via the algebra transitivity lemma.

difficulty_reason: For a factorization X -> Y -> Z with X -> Y a complete intersection morphism, the lemma produces the canonical distinguished triangle f^*NL_{Y/Z} -> NL_{X/Z} -> NL_{X/Y} -> f^*NL_{Y/Z}[1] in D(O_X) recovering the six-term exact sequence. The proof is a written two-step reduction: it identifies the triangle with the vanishing of a canonical map, reduces via the six-term sequence to injectivity on H^{-1} of a specific map, and then verifies that injectivity affine locally by translating through the affine NL lemma and citing the algebra transitivity result for lci morphisms. Retained author proof at lines 3945-3958.
